scope: Five previously untested cases: two supplied reviews, three synthetic. One live run per case, existing retry bound, no tuning.

cases.review_text: Mmmm, this cake was so good. I made it exactly as directed except I used a different frosting only because I had some leftover from another cake. The next time I make this I will add one more cup of apples because more is better right?!
expected_behavior: Recognize the different frosting as actually used, but unspecified: ask which frosting/ingredients/amounts; do not invent a frosting recipe.
Adding one more cup of apples is a future plan, not a tested change. Keep the original 2 cups apples.
Return the original recipe with zero edits and a needs_clarification status. Preserve both the tried frosting change and the future apple idea in the analysis.
Do not invent benefits or assert that more apples improves the recipe.

cases.review_text: Overall it was pretty good but the measurements were way off. HAS to be a typo. 1/4lb of meat to serve 4??? I used a lil over 1lb and it even then it was swimming in the broth. After following the recipe, i added extra soy and sugar only because i thought the flavor was a little on the lite side. Overall good.** If you cant find dashi, beef broth/stock works just fine. My japanese mom happen to have some so i was able to get some from her.
expected_behavior: Retain three tried changes separately: a little over 1 lb beef, extra soy sauce, and extra sugar.
Beef amount is approximate: preserve the qualifier if applied, or explicitly defer it. Do not silently convert to exactly 1 lb or a guessed precise amount.
Extra soy and sugar have no measured amounts: ask about each, and do not guess quantities.
The beef-stock suggestion is conditional advice, not evidence of a tried substitution: the reviewer says they obtained dashi from their mother. Keep the original dashi and do not add beef broth.

An unchanged needs_clarification recipe is acceptable if all three tried changes and the untested advice are retained. If only approximate beef is safely applied, label the unresolved remainder and keep ingredient/direction references consistent.
No unrelated modifications or invented benefits.

cases.provenance: Synthetic held-out case authored before this run; not a supplied community review.

recipe.title: Simple dairy porridge
instructions: Combine dairy milk and rolled oats in a saucepan.

cases.review_text: I used 1 cup oat milk instead of dairy milk and simmered for 8 minutes instead of 10. I kept the honey exactly as written.
expected_behavior: Apply exactly two changes: 1 cup oat milk replaces 1 cup dairy milk, and simmer for 8 minutes instead of 10.
Update the milk ingredient and its use in the first instruction; remove all dairy-milk references.
Keep oats, honey, stirring, and serving unchanged. Keeping honey is not an additional modification.
No claimed flavor/health/texture benefit: the review states none.

recipe.title: Sauteed zucchini
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.
Add zucchini and saute for 5 minutes.

cases.review_text: I used 1 tablespoon olive oil, not 2. I did not add butter. Next time I might add garlic.
expected_behavior: Apply only the olive-oil reduction: 2 tablespoons to 1 tablespoon in both the ingredient and the heating instruction.
Do not add butter or list it as a tried addition: the statement explicitly negates it.
Garlic is an untried future idea; keep it in the analysis but do not apply it or invent an amount.
Keep zucchini, salt, cooking time and other actions unchanged. No invented benefits.

recipe.title: Two-sugar crumble
instructions: Combine white sugar and brown sugar with oats.
Rub in butter, then bake at 180 C for 20 minutes.

cases.review_text: I used 1/2 cup sugar and it worked well.
expected_behavior: The recipe has two distinct sugars and the review does not identify which was reduced or whether 1/2 cup was the combined total.
Retain the quantity proposal as needs_clarification and ask which sugar/total. Do not guess white or brown sugar.
Keep all ingredients and instructions unchanged, with zero applied/reported edits.
The only outcome evidence is the reviewer saying it worked well; do not invent a specific texture/health explanation.
